pins.name: GPIO6
pins.label: GPIO6
pins.notes:
PIN_SERVO1 — onboard servo header 1 signal line. #define only in pins_arduino.h (no static-const alias), so added here to expose it as a usable general-purpose PWM/digital output for driving a hobby servo — confirmed via examples/lib/explorer.py (SERVO_1_PIN=const(9)... note vendor numbering is servo-1=GPIO9..servo-4=GPIO6, reversed from the header's own PIN_SERVO1..4=6..9 naming; both sources agree on the *set* {6,7,8,9} being the four servo headers) and product-page 'servo headers' feature. Matches pimoroni_servo2040 precedent (servo-header PWM outputs kept general-purpose, not exclusionary).
Check if available on board

pins.name: GPIO12
pins.label: GPIO12
pins.notes:
PIN_PWM_AUDIO — onboard piezo speaker PWM drive line. #define only (no static-const alias), added here as general-purpose digital/PWM output so a Designer sketch can generate tones — confirmed via examples/lib/explorer.py (PWM_AUDIO_PIN=const(12)) and product copy ('integrated speaker'). No dedicated 'buzzer' capability vocabulary exists in this codebase; matches the cytron_maker_pi_rp2040 PIN_BUZZER precedent of leaving such a pin general-purpose rather than excluding it.

pins.name: SWITCH_C
pins.label: GPIO14 (Button)
pins.notes: SWITCH_C — one of six onboard tactile buttons surrounding the LCD. Confirmed via this board's own pins_arduino.h alias, examples/lib/explorer.py (SWITCH_C_PIN=const(14)), and docs/reference.md ('The buttons are Active Low. So you'll read 0 when the button is being pressed'). Input-only (digital_input+button), matching this repo's adafruit_macropad2040 KEY1-12 precedent for simple ground-referenced tactile switches.

pins.name: SWITCH_BOOT
pins.label: GPIO22 (Button)
pins.notes: SWITCH_BOOT — onboard User/Boot button, confirmed via this board's own pins_arduino.h alias (comment: "Boot button, also referred to as the user switch") and examples/lib/explorer.py/docs/reference.md, which read it identically (same Active-Low Pin mechanism) to SWITCH_A-Z alongside a separate 'Reset' button. No vendor source documents special diode/strap circuitry for this pin (unlike the RP2040 Pico's QSPI-CS-based BOOTSEL magic pin, which is out of scope entirely) — tagged input-only (digital_input+button), matching this repo's conservative adafruit_macropad2040 ENCODER_SWITCH/BOOT precedent rather than assuming full output safety.
